To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

photon elastic-scattering at high energy and low momentum transfer scales with energy and that the violation of scaling in the Delbrück scattering experiments is due to the dependence of the effective coupling constant on momentum transfer.
the photon elastic scattering amplitude scales with energy at high energy and that the violation of scaling can be contained in the momentum transfer dependence of the coupling constants.
the elastic scattering amplitude for photons scales with energy at high energy and at fixed scattering angle, and the violation of this scaling is due to the momentum dependence of the coupling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: How can we use the high-energy behaviour of the photon elastic-scattered amplitude to learn about the structure of the electron?
the study of the high-energy behavior of the elastic scattering amplitudes for photons and electrons.
the elastic scattering of high-energy photons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for photon elastic scattering at high energy, the scaling hypothesis holds for all irreducible diagrams, but not for the complete amplitude.

the photon elastic scattering amplitude is not scale invariant, and the violation of scale invariance is contained entirely in its dependence on the momentum transfer, and is independent of the energy.

the photon elastic scattering amplitudes corresponding only to reducible diagrams scale as the photon energy approaches infinity with scattering angle fixed, and that the violation of scaling, which is observed in experiment, is contained entirely in coupling-constant dependence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photon elastic scattering at high energy is dominated by the lowest order diagram.
the photon elastic scattering amplitudes at high energy and at fixed angle are not universal, i.e., they depend on the coupling constant and on the momentum transfer in addition to energy and angle.
, if the electron and photon coupling constants are independent of the momentum transfer, then the photon elastic-scatter amplitudes at high energy scale as the energy increases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photon elastic amplitudes are very different from those of the charged lepton.
, at high energy, the photon elastic-scatter cross-section is dominated by the lowest-order Feynman diagram, the Born amplitude.
the violation of scaling in the elastic scattering of photons at high energy is a very weak effect, and that the scaling behaviour is a very good approximation.
